Axios Pro Rata
By Dan Primack · Sep 14, 2026
 
 
Top of the Morning
 

Illustration: Brendan Lynch/Axios
 

Anthropic is still likely to go public in 2026, even as AI safety rockets into the zeitgeist, per multiple sources.

The big picture: A lot has changed in AI land since last Friday's newsletter, but the IPO calendar isn't one of them.

  • There have been social media suggestions that Anthropic might want to wait, due to new product liability and regulation questions.
  • Yet the Claude maker might actually view the past 48 hours as elevating the case for its IPO rather than dampening it — arguing that safety is improved via the transparency of being a public company.
  • OpenAI, meanwhile, was leaning toward a 2027 listing and still seems to be doing so.

Zoom in: Neither Anthropic's business nor the investor FOMO are different this week than last.

  • Yes, Anthropic has pledged to have third-party evaluation of its models, and suggested some pacing that might slow new model releases. But so did its top rival, and there's still an insane amount of untapped revenue tied to models already in market.
  • It's also not like Anthropic would be the first or only listed frontier lab, as Alphabet and SpaceX shares continue to trade.
  • There's also a cynical argument that "pacing" could reduce Anthropic's compute spend, thus improving its financials. Some also have accused the company of pursuing a policy of regulatory capture — and if you buy that argument, you'll probably also buy Anthropic stock.
  • Finally, it still needs the money. It could delay and raise more via private markets, but no frontier lab can just sit on the capital markets sidelines.

Driving the news: Anthropic has decided to list on the Nasdaq, per Business Insider.

Yes, but: One thing that could change Anthropic's course would be if there's a major unwinding of the AI trade.

  • Stocks did open lower this morning, but not drastically so. And it's tough to parse how much pullback is caused by AI tumult versus oil prices and interest rates.

The bottom line: Want to own a piece of Claude while also making a bet on the future of humanity? You'll be able to. Soon.
 
 
The BFD
 

Illustration: Aïda Amer/Axios
 

Sequence Holdings and DFO Management (Michael Dell's family office) have agreed to acquire Baldwin Insurance Group (Nasdaq: BWIN) for $7.7 billion.

Why it's the BFD: This is an AI spin on insurance industry consolidation, which is moving fast and furious.

Catch up quick: Sequence is a VC-backed, permanent holding company that buys established enterprises in the services industry and then uses AI to further modernize them.

  • Its first major deal was for BankSouth, and it's also said to be looking at health care. Backers include 8VC, Conviction, and Lux Capital.

Behind the scenes: DFO is investing directly in the Baldwin deal and also is becoming an investor in Sequence.

By the numbers: Baldwin stockholders will receive $32.50 per share in cash, which represents a 9.6% premium on Friday's close and an 88% premium on where Baldwin traded before initial media reports of a possible deal.

  • Baldwin has traded as high as $32.59 (Aug. 24) and as low as $15.88 (Feb. 12) over the past year.

The bottom line: "Baldwin specialises in commercial insurance brokerage, advising midsized and large companies shopping for insurance policies for everything from cyber security to employee benefits to real estate." — Antoine Gara & Eric Platt, FT
 
 
Venture Capital Deals
 

🚀 Open Cosmos, a U.K. satellite maker, raised £300m from Lightrock, ETF Partners, Institut Català de Finances, Entrepreneurs First, Convex Group, National Security Strategic Investment Fund, Phoenix Court, and Claret Capital Partners. axios.link/4cIVQry

• Tabby, a Saudi BNPL company, raised $233m in Series F funding at a $6.5b valuation led by insider Blue Pool Capital. Other backers include HSG, Wellington Management, and Arbor Ventures. axios.link/4AdiJgS

🚀 Firehawk Aerospace, a Dallas-based maker of rocket motors, is in talks to raise up to $200m at a $1.25b valuation led by Rochefort Asset Management and joined by insider 1789 Capital, per Bloomberg. axios.link/4cGEcVt

🚑 Tandem Health, a Swedish medical scribe startup, raised $100m in Series B funding. Scaleup Europe Fund led, joined by Kinnevik, Northzone, Amino Collective, and Visionaries. axios.link/4j25kC6

• BRKZ, a Saudi building materials procurement platform, raised $13m in Series B equity funding. Wa'ed Ventures and 500 Global led, joined by BECO Capital and ANB Capital. It also secured an $18m debt facility from Stride Ventures. axios.link/46YgjoQ

🚑 Shennon Biotechnologies, an SF-based developer of precision immunotherapies for cancer, raised $12m from Future Ventures, NextGen Venture Partners, Samos Investments, Atypical Ventures, Saras Capital, DCVC, Foundation Capital, and AV8 Ventures. axios.link/4h3uGNd

• Chift, a Brussels-based financial connectivity startup, raised €10.5m in Series A funding. BlackFin Capital Partners led, joined by Entourage, Shapers, Seeder Fund, and Wallonie Entreprendre. axios.link/4xm3zTO

🚑 Nara Health, a third-party administrator, raised $10m in seed funding led by Khosla Ventures, per Axios Pro. axios.link/46rZXon

• Mecka AI, a humanoid robotics training startup, is in talks to raise funding led by Sequoia Capital at a $500m valuation, per TechCrunch. axios.link/4hojtbA

Private Equity Deals
 

🚑 Apollo is in talks to buy orthopedics business DePuy Synthes from Johnson & Johnson (NYSE: JNJ) for around $20b, per Bloomberg. axios.link/4gO4k38

• Blackstone agreed to acquire Flow Control Holdings, a Cincinnati-based provider of flow control solutions and components, from Audax Private Equity (which retains a minority stake). axios.link/46UpYNd

🚑 CVC Capital Partners is in talks to buy the mainland China unit of contact lens maker Ginko International from EQT for $700m-$800m (including debt), per Reuters. axios.link/4yw3AWg

🚑 Danforth Health, an Avesi Partners portfolio company, acquired Ambit RD, a Morristown, N.J.-based provider of patient identification services for biopharma. axios.link/4h6csuP

• Francisco Partners and KKR agreed to buy a combined 15% stake in TeamSystem, an Italian business software firm owned by Hellman & Friedman, per Reuters. axios.link/4is3AC6

• Genstar Capital invested in Richey May, a Denver-based accounting and advisory firm, with participation from Aksia. axios.link/4AhmbXW

🚑 Ivy Fertility, backed by InTandem Capital Partners, acquired Santa Barbara Fertility Center. axios.link/4yVnsT9

• Main Capital Partners agreed to buy British education software firm Tribal (AIM: TRB) for £189m. axios.link/4AdB8dr

• Pacific West, backed by Bluejay Capital Partners, acquired Coleman, a Kansas City-based provider of construction and repair services for rail and industrial facilities. axios.link/4yAHi5U

• Waterland said it's continuing to consider a takeover offer for U.K. telco Gamma Communications (LSE: GAMA), which recently agreed to sell to Epris for around £1b, but that it's no longer working in concert with Inflexion-backed Giacom. axios.link/4ri4RxW
 
 
Public Offerings
 

Three companies plan to price U.S. IPOs this week: Holtec, Orion180 Insurance Group, and American Savings Bank.

• Bamboo Insurance Services, a Midvale, Utah-based homeowners insurer backed by CVC Capital Partners and White Mountains, set IPO terms to 35m shares at $18-$20. It reports $14m of net income on $173m in revenue for the first half of 2026, and plans to list on the NYSE (BMB). axios.link/4xsIAim

🚑 Electra Therapeutics, an SF-based biotech focused on immunology and cancer, set IPO terms to 21.67m shares at $14-$16. It would have a $917m market cap at the midpoint, plans to list on the Nasdaq (ETRA), and has raised $300m from OrbiMed (9% pre-IPO stake), Westlake BioPartners (7.1%), Redmile (7.1%), Aventus (6.2%), EQT LSP (6.2%), and New Leaf Ventures (4.4%). axios.link/46Up6YX

• Kioxia (Tokyo: 285A), a Japanese memory storage firm whose backers include Bain Capital, is speaking to bankers about a $10b U.S. float, per Bloomberg. axios.link/4h3pmcH
 
 
Liquidity Events
 

🚑 GE HealthCare (Nasdaq: GEHC) is in talks to buy Sofie Biosciences, a Dulles, Va.-based maker of cancer scan chemicals, for around $1b, per the FT. Sofie backers include Trilantic. axios.link/4h5M2ta

⚡ Trillium Flow Technologies, a First Reserve portfolio company, agreed to sell its U.S. pumps business to Crane Co. (NYSE: CR) for approximately $240m. axios.link/3VcSuXL
 
 
More M&A
 

• Colgate-Palmolive (NYSE: CL) hired Goldman Sachs to explore the sale of several mass-market consumer brands — including Softsoap, Irish Spring, and Speed Stick — per Reuters. axios.link/4dCrG9I

• Larry Ellison scrapped plans to sell up to $7.5b of Oracle (Nasdaq: ORCL) stock, just one day after Oracle disclosed the plans. axios.link/4xNUJzb

⚡ Essar Energy Transition Fuels agreed to buy U.K. fuel retailer SGN Retail. axios.link/4xk0tzF

• Sazerac, the New Orleans maker of Southern Comfort and Buzzballz, acquired U.K. spirits brand Au Vodka. axios.link/4AdAa0Q

• Solar Industries of India agreed to buy South African chemicals and mining firm Omnia Holdings (JSE: OMN) for around $1.36b in cash. axios.link/4xjutf3

• SThree (LSE: STEMS), a U.K. recruiting firm, rejected a preliminary takeover approach from Circle8 Group (Nasdaq: CIRC). axios.link/46nPj1X
 
 
It's Personnel
 

• Brian DeFee joined Equitex as a managing director and head of Americas capital formation. He previously was with Capstone Partners. axios.link/4yzyOM6

• Julia Liuson joined Permira as a Menlo Park-based senior advisor. She is the former president of Microsoft's developer division. axios.link/4ytrLES

• Matt Shafer joined Golub Capital as a managing director and head of the firm's GP-led private equity secondaries strategy. He previously was with Northleaf Capital Partners. axios.link/4xWBvYo

• William Sonneborn joined Hunter Point Capital as president and COO. He previously was president of Generate Capital. axios.link/4AaPqvt
 
 
In Memoriam: Bill Draper
 

William Draper III
 

William Draper III, a pioneer of Silicon Valley venture capital, has died at the age of 98.

  • After college and military service, Draper and his father founded the West Coast's first venture capital firm. He later partnered with Pitch Johnson to form Sutter Hill Ventures and then, following a second career in public service, would found Draper International.
  • He also is the father of venture capitalist Tim Draper and grandfather of venture capitalist Jesse Draper.

What Jesse Draper wrote, in part: "What he did and helped create in Silicon Valley is immeasurable, but whenever he was given credit, he would pass it off to Leland Stanford ... Family came first, a lesson he taught us all ... He was at every major event in my life, cheering and standing with a hand in the air, from my high school graduation to college graduation..."

  • "He was fiercely competitive when it came to chess, tennis, and just about any other game. He had a bowl of chocolate ice cream every day and often declared, 'Hot fudge sundaes all around!' I was lucky enough to say goodbye to him on my grandmother's birthday, the day before he passed, and to witness his final words with my aunt. Believe it or not, they were: 'Ice cream.'"
